requirement:
The requirements index MUST link to its execution-coverage subchapter under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`.
rationale:
**Obligation.** `requirements.test-coverage.index.navigation` has one obligation: the requirements index chapter must link to its generated execution-coverage subchapter. `requirements.test-coverage.index`, which it cites, is context only.

**Test.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It builds a book whose requirements index is `reports.md` and calls `populate_in`, the production entry point marked `{impl}`. It asserts that the index chapter's content contains `[Coverage gaps](reports/coverage.html)`. That assertion checks both the link text and the href to the generated chapter, whose path the test also asserts is `reports/coverage.md`.

**Input classes.** The test runs the index both with a section number (`Some(3.2)`) and without one (`None`). The link assertion holds in both cases. I read `populate_in`. It appends the link to the chapter whose path matches `parent`, and it returns an error if no such chapter exists. No other condition affects the link, so the two numbering cases cover the distinctions that matter.

**Other tests.** `references` shows no other test or implementation site for this requirement. A nested index path is not an input class the requirement distinguishes. Whether the index was explicitly placed or automatically generated is covered by the cited `requirements.test-coverage.index`, so I did not assess it here.

I found no gap.
